pure-announcement.rationale: A tutorial teaching an architecture for long-running agents, not a launch or release note, even though it demonstrates on Google's ADK stack throughout.

duplicate.rationale: No nearest concept covers durable long-running agent execution; context-layer and the MCP concepts address different layers.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Complete runnable source is linked and each claimed pattern is demonstrated in code a reader can execute.

durability.rationale: The core patterns — explicit persisted state machines instead of chat-history state, event-driven wake-up with atomic state deltas, and the three named failure modes of stateless agents over idle time — transfer beyond ADK and will still hold in twelve months.

actionability.rationale: It gives a reproducible recipe — state schema injected into the system prompt, tools as checkpointing transitions, webhook-driven resumption, pre-seeded evals that simulate idle time — that changes how someone would build workflow agents in any framework.

atomicity.rationale: The checkpoint-and-resume architecture is one paragraph-statable idea, but the note bundles it with two separable practices the source itself headlines — sub-agent delegation and golden-eval simulation of multi-day flows — that are distinct findings.
